messages:
maria: Observed a latency spike for seq_len=64 bursts around 09:12 UTC. CUTLASS path gets rejected and we fall back to Triton, which increases tail latency for small batches. Anyone else seeing probe rejections?

kevin: saw the same in canary. logs show repeated probe failures then a fallback. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:05Z] probe=seq64 model=rw-7B kernel=cuda-cutlass status=reject reason=\"smem_overflow\"
[2026-03-18T09:12:05Z] probe=seq64 fallback=triton kernel=triton_op latency_ms=24
[2026-03-18T09:12:05Z] kvhit=true batch=3 note=\"kv-affinity-mismatch\"
```

natalie: FYI autoscaler change yesterday increased micro-batching for multi-tenant pools. KV cache warming is now sparser per-worker — could change probe statistics.

jon: runtime-bot reported a rollout: 
runtime-bot: deploy: feature=probe-sample-damping value=0.6 rolled to prod at 08:50 UTC :rocket:

kevin: my hypothesis: damping reduced effective probe sample size so single noisy rejects cause immediate kernel switch. Two quick mitigation ideas: raise consecutive-accept threshold OR decrease damping (increase sample rate).

maria: minimal repro (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"X-SeqLen: 64\" -d '{"prompt":"hello\n"}'
```

kevin: easy profiling command if you want to grab a trace locally: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o seq64_trace ./redwood_serve --model rw-7B --seq 64` — look for smem and launch failures around probe windows.

natalie: quick metric from yesterday vs today: cutlass_accept_rate: 45% -> 12% after damping. probe_reject_reasons: smem_overflow (60%), out_of_registers (25%), other (15%).

maria: would adding hysteresis help? e.g., require N consecutive successes before switching kernel, and M consecutive failures before switching back.

jon: +1. Also canary rollback option if we want a fast fix. ops-bot can we schedule a rollback?

ops-bot: rollback scheduled in 5m for feature=probe-sample-damping. I'll post status when done.

kevin: long-term: augment autotune with seq-length conditional probes and kv-aware routing. If KV cache indicates cold state, bias towards Triton until cache warms. That avoids repeated flip-flopping for small-batch cold-starts.

natalie: agree. Also adding a probe-scoped budget counter per-worker (max probes per minute) prevents noisy bursts from destabilizing kernel selection.

maria: I'll attach the nsys traces and the tail-latency graphs to the incident and open an autotune task: \"seq64-kernel-hysteresis-and-kv-affinity\". tagging: @kevin @natalie @jon

jon: thx. once rollback completes we'll validate tail p95. If good, promote a fix with conservative hysteresis and bump probe sample back up. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team — monitoring p95 now. will update thread when traces are uploaded. :eyes:
